messages:
maria: FYI customer ACME reported intermittent 429s during short bursts. They see latency spikes and then a flurry of rate_limit errors even though monthly quota is fine. Mostly on lots of tiny chat turns.

devon: can you paste the raw response / headers they captured? 429 body + x-rate-limit headers would help. :eyes:

maria: they sent this snippet:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 167
{
  \"error\": \"rate_limited\",
  \"message\": \"Request rejected due to short-term burst limits\"
}
```

maria: timeline: steady ~200 rps, but micro-bursts where many clients send 2-4 token prompts simultaneously (chat). They run continuous batching + KV cache for persona prefixes.

alex: sounds like batching + token-bucket interplay. If some requests miss the KV cache and take longer, that raises in-flight time, reduces effective throughput and the burst window empties -> perceived throttle.

sanjay: yep. KV cache cold misses can add ~20-50ms depending on prefix prep. With continuous batching that increases batch latency and reduces completed requests/sec.

devon: ask them for SDK call + config and to enable these metrics: inflight_requests, batch_size_histogram, kvcache_hit_rate (per-prefix), and per-route_rate_limit_rejects. If they can reproduce, get pprof traces from the serving node.

maria: they shared repro curl:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"rwd-chat-1\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}],\"max_tokens\":16}'
```

maria: they said disabling continuous batching stopped the 429s but p95 latency worsened, so it's definitely a batching+cache interaction.

devon: quick mitigation/debug items I recommend:
- collect batch_size_hist and batch_latency spans around failure windows
- inspect kvcache_hit_rate per-prefix to spot high-miss prefixes
- temporarily bump their account burst capacity by ~2x to confirm throttling is burst-limited
- enable kvcache_prefetch or explicitly warm common prefixes on deploy
- reduce batch_timeout_ms slightly to trade throughput for lower tail latency

alex: also advise client-side jittered backoff + honor Retry-After. But that's a workaround; root is cache coldstart causing longer service times and backlog.

infra-sre: if they can reproduce we can grab pprof from the node serving them. Example:

```
curl -s \"http://internal-admin:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=10\" > profile.pb
# upload to S3 and share
```

sanjay: suggested SDK config (pseudocode):

```
client = RedwoodClient(API_KEY)
client.configure(
  continuous_batching=True,
  batch_timeout_ms=20,    # tighten tail
  max_concurrency_per_worker=24,
  kvcache_prefetch=True,
  kvcache_warmup_prefixes=[\"user_profile:\"]
)
```

maria: ACME applied kvcache_warmup + increased batch concurrency; 429s dropped immediately while keeping continuous batching. p95 rose a bit but stayed within SLA.

devon: long-term platform fixes to consider:
- bump default token-bucket burst capacity for short-chat routes
- add alert/metric for \"kvcache_miss_spike\" correlated with rate-limit rejects
- implement hot-prefix warmup after model rollouts to avoid cold waves

alex: we should audit the quota enforcement model. We use per-account token buckets with refill/sec and a max-burst. When service times increase (due to cold cache), queues form and refill doesn't keep up even though tokens aren't over monthly quota -> causes rejections. Simulate in loadtest harness.

maria: customer logs show kvcache_hit_rate rose from 46% -> 94% after warmup. No more 429s in the previous failure window. Marking support side resolved pending infra-sre runbook.

support-bot: ticket #C-8421 transitioned to status: awaiting-sre (assignee: infra-sre)

infra-sre: pulling traces now. I'll draft a short runbook for prod ops: recommended defaults for batch_timeout_ms and burst_bucket sizes for chat short-turn workloads.

maria: thanks everyone. cc @devon for postmortem notes. Closing from support after infra-sre confirms runbook posted. :thumbsup:
